issue.title: gateway: an allowed_tools tool_choice is dropped before the Grok plugin can read it
issue.body:
Found while re-reviewing magpie-community/plugins#263 (Grok's opt-in native X search).

A Responses request to the Grok plugin with `tool_choice: {"type":"allowed_tools", ...}` reaches the plugin's `fetch` with no `tool_choice` at all. `grokPluginBody` → `grokShaped` (internal/provider/grok.go) drops a `tool_choice` object whose type isn't in `grokTools`, the same as `grokBody` does for the built-in. So the plugin can't tell an `allowed_tools` choice from no choice.

With the X search option on (grok ≥ 0.2.0), that request is sent `tools: [..., {"type":"x_search"}]`: a tool outside the client's allowed list. Seen through the real gateway at ba319a758 with a fake Grok upstream:

```
POST /v1/responses {"tool_choice":{"type":"allowed_tools","mode":"auto","tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file"}]},"tools":[{read_file}]}
-> upstream: {"tools":[{read_file},{"type":"x_search"}]}   (no tool_choice)
```

The plugin itself handles it (its unit test passes `allowed_tools` and adds nothing), and every plugin version since the TOOLS filter drops an unsupported `tool_choice` object before Grok. So the fix is on magpie's side, like #3110: `grokPluginBody` keeps an unsupported `tool_choice` object for the plugin to read and drop. The option is off by default, and magpie already loses `allowed_tools`' restriction on function tools for Grok, so the impact is small.

## Source & environment

yetone/magpie#3153, opened and diagnosed by yetone (0 comments at the time of writing): a `tool_choice` object the Grok plugin should read is dropped before its `fetch`, so with the plugin's X search option on (grok 0.2.0) a request goes out with `x_search` over a client's `allowed_tools`. The issue quotes a repro through the real gateway at ba319a758 with a fake Grok upstream. Fixed from f5b0157420a4491f6e707b49a8af8e87ea8050a1 (upstream/main), one commit, on macOS arm64 with the repo's Go toolchain.

## Minimal repro

A Responses request relayed to the Grok plugin in its own protocol, tools present, the client allowing `read_file` alone:

```
POST /v1/responses {"tool_choice":{"type":"allowed_tools","mode":"auto","tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file"}]},"tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file"}]}
-> plugin's fetch: the body with no tool_choice at all (grokShaped dropped the object)
-> Grok:            {"tools":[{read_file},{"type":"x_search"}]}
```

The plugin can't tell an `allowed_tools` choice from no preference, so it adds `x_search` and a tool outside the client's allowed list goes out. The same drop is pinned by the new test against `grokPluginBody` before the fix: `plugin: tool_choice {Type: Mode: Tools:[]}`.

## Root cause

`grokShaped` (internal/provider/grok.go) shapes every Grok-bound body: `grokBody` for the built-in and `grokPluginBody` for the plugin's accounts (`a.body` in internal/provider/plugins.go, applied at each `forward` through `Provider.Prepare`). With tools present it drops a `tool_choice` object whose `type` isn't in `grokTools` — `allowed_tools` among them. That is right for the built-in, which is Grok's last stop (the backend turns the request away over a tool_choice it doesn't know), and wrong for the plugin: the object holds the client's restriction, and the plugin is the one reader that honors it (its own unit test passes `allowed_tools` and adds nothing; every version since the TOOLS filter leaves an unsupported `tool_choice` object out before Grok, per the issue). #3110 set the shape for the lone `"none"`: magpie hands the plugin what it reads, the plugin decides what Grok sees.

## Fix

`grokShaped` keeps an unsupported `tool_choice` object on the plugin path; the built-in still drops it. `grokShaped`'s `keepNone` is `forPlugin` now, since keeping is no longer only about `"none"`. The comments on `grokPluginBody` and at the drop point, the Grok mover's `min` note (internal/provider/migrate_side.go, no bump: the min version's TOOLS filter already drops such an object before Grok) and the Grok plugin paragraph in docs/subsystems/provider-plugins.md say so. One commit, five files, +61 -11; no dependency, no unrelated change.

## Source & environment

yetone/magpie#3153, opened and diagnosed by yetone (0 comments at the time of writing): a `tool_choice` object the Grok plugin should read is dropped before its `fetch`, so with the plugin's X search option on (grok 0.2.0) a request goes out with `x_search` over a client's `allowed_tools`. The issue quotes a repro through the real gateway at ba319a758 with a fake Grok upstream. Fixed from f5b0157420a4491f6e707b49a8af8e87ea8050a1 (upstream/main), one commit, on macOS arm64 with the repo's Go toolchain.

## Minimal repro

A Responses request relayed to the Grok plugin in its own protocol, tools present, the client allowing `read_file` alone:

```
POST /v1/responses {"tool_choice":{"type":"allowed_tools","mode":"auto","tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file"}]},"tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file"}]}
-> plugin's fetch: the body with no tool_choice at all (grokShaped dropped the object)
-> Grok:            {"tools":[{read_file},{"type":"x_search"}]}
```

The plugin can't tell an `allowed_tools` choice from no preference, so it adds `x_search` and a tool outside the client's allowed list goes out. The same drop is pinned by the new test against `grokPluginBody` before the fix: `plugin: tool_choice {Type: Mode: Tools:[]}`.

## Root cause

`grokShaped` (internal/provider/grok.go) shapes every Grok-bound body: `grokBody` for the built-in and `grokPluginBody` for the plugin's accounts (`a.body` in internal/provider/plugins.go, applied at each `forward` through `Provider.Prepare`). With tools present it drops a `tool_choice` object whose `type` isn't in `grokTools` — `allowed_tools` among them. That is right for the built-in, which is Grok's last stop (the backend turns the request away over a tool_choice it doesn't know), and wrong for the plugin: the object holds the client's restriction, and the plugin is the one reader that honors it (its own unit test passes `allowed_tools` and adds nothing; every version since the TOOLS filter leaves an unsupported `tool_choice` object out before Grok, per the issue). #3110 set the shape for the lone `"none"`: magpie hands the plugin what it reads, the plugin decides what Grok sees.

## Fix

`grokShaped` keeps an unsupported `tool_choice` object on the plugin path; the built-in still drops it. `grokShaped`'s `keepNone` is `forPlugin` now, since keeping is no longer only about `"none"`. The comments on `grokPluginBody` and at the drop point, the Grok mover's `min` note (internal/provider/migrate_side.go, no bump: the min version's TOOLS filter already drops such an object before Grok) and the Grok plugin paragraph in docs/subsystems/provider-plugins.md say so. issue.title: gateway: server-managed tools (web_search/web_fetch) silently dropped on translated routes — 200 OK, no error or capability signal

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

When a request carries provider-hosted (server-managed) tool declarations — e.g. Anthropic `web_search_20260209` / `web_fetch_20250910` on `/v1/messages`, or OpenAI `{type:"web_search"}` on `/v1/responses` — magpie forwards them correctly when the upstream protocol supports them, but **silently drops them** when the resolved upstream is OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible. The request returns 200, the model answers as if it has no tools, and nothing in the response or logs marks the drop.

The dangerous consequence: the model cannot distinguish "no tool configured" from "tool was stripped", so it answers anyway — including confidently hallucinated facts (observed: `swe-2` reported today's date as **May 22, 2026** when it was actually October 21).

## Environment

magpie 0.1.1312 (macOS), gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`. Verified by direct SSE probing of the local gateway.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Server-managed tool silently dropped (upstream = openai-compatible plugin provider)
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $MAGPIE_KEY" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{
    "model": "devin/claude-fable-5-1",
    "max_tokens": 1024, "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"What is today'"'"'s date? Search the web."}],
    "tools": [{"type":"web_search_20260209","name":"web_search","max_uses":5}]
  }'
# -> streams only a `text` block; model replies "I don't have the ability to search the web"
```

Control — a normal function tool on the same route works fine (model emits `tool_use`), so tool *forwarding* is not broken in general:

```bash
# same body but tools: [{"name":"get_weather", ...}], tool_choice forced
# -> devin/claude-fable-5-1, devin/swe-2, deepseek/deepseek-flash all emit tool_use blocks
```

## Measured behavior matrix

| Upstream provider | Upstream protocol | Function tools | `web_search_*` | `web_fetch_*` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `codex` (Codex OAuth) | Responses | — | ✅ full `web_search_call` lifecycle | n/a |
| `deepseek` → `api.deepseek.com/anthropic` | Anthropic Messages | ✅ | ✅ real `server_tool_use` + `web_search_tool_result` | ❌ upstream 422 (unsupported tool type — correctly surfaces an error!) |
| `right-code` → `rightapi.ai` | Anthropic Messages (relay) | ✅ | ❌ dropped (relay-side, both `20250305` and `20260209`) | ✅ `20250910` and `20260309` both work |
| `devin` plugin → `server.codeium.com/devin/v1` | OpenAI Chat Completions | ✅ | ❌ silently dropped | ❌ silently dropped |
| `opencode-zen-free` plugin → `opencode.ai/inference/v1` | OpenAI Chat Completions | — | ❌ silently dropped (both `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`) | ❌ silently dropped |

Two observations worth noting:

- The DeepSeek 422 response (`unknown variant 'web_fetch_20250910'`) reached the client verbatim — proof that on Anthropic-routed providers magpie forwards the `tools` array unchanged, and proof that **surfacing an upstream error works** when the upstream produces one.
- The same `/v1/messages` entry point therefore behaves completely differently per model — invisible to clients. A Claude-named model served over an openai-compatible upstream cannot carry Anthropic-native tools, but nothing tells the client that.

## Expected behavior

Any of the following would fix the silent-degradation problem (my preference: 1 + 3):

1. **Fail or warn on stripped tools.** When translation to the upstream protocol drops entries from `tools`, either reject with a 4xx naming the dropped tool types, or annotate the response (metadata field / SSE event / synthetic `tool_result` error block). A silent 200 that removes capabilities is the worst possible signal.
2. **Echo dropped entries back** in the response (e.g. an `x-magpie-stripped-tools` header or a `stripped_tools` field) so clients can detect degradation without deep-parsing the stream.
3. **Expose capability metadata in `/v1/models`** — e.g. a `server_tools: ["web_search","web_fetch"]` list per model — so agent harnesses can avoid configuring tools that can never execute.

## Why it matters

Agent CLIs now reach provider-native web tools through this gateway (pi extensions, Claude Code-style flows, Grok X search per #3153). A client that sends `web_search` and gets a clean 200 with the tool silently removed gets not just a worse answer — it gets a *confidently wrong* one, with no way to detect that the tool never ran. The fix doesn't require implementing hosted search where the upstream lacks it; it only requires making the drop visible.
